hypothesis: Repair the two mandatory t000068 validation failures while preserving its narrow extension: already recognized canonical, finite-count unconditional reductions over acyclic producers may use bounded chunks. A consumer certificate selected from the actual emitted CFG can establish local iteration/control and reduction/result edges for scalar consumers, scalar fallbacks, vector tails and EVL separately. No production C++ changes, recognition extensions, profitability model, corpus edits or extra FP assumptions are introduced in this repair.
semantics: The consumer certificate now checks complete typed PHIs against actual predecessor sets, zero scalar entry or vector-rounded resume, the unit next ordinal, next-versus-chunk-count inequality, true backedge and false exit, the producer-independent scratch GEPs/loads, both integer operand orders and ordered FP update, nonidentity chunk seeds, backedge carries and final observable result forwarding. It runs for every emitted scalar consumer regardless of requested scalar/EVL policy, including C=1; vector tails instead certify zero/n.vec resume edges and resumed reductions. Vector control certifies the local count guard, local urem/sub rounding, zero index and exact VF increments/exit; EVL instead certifies local AVL, selected length, VP masks/lengths, merged integer accumulators and no scalar tail. A bounded typed PHI walk follows only real single-predecessor middle/LCSSA bridges before final chunk and original exit results. Existing operation/branch/state/export/provenance checks and the failing total-N mutation remain. The integration certificate now accepts an explicit capacity and checks the cross-edge chunk schedule without skipping original non-latch branches. Exact original IR, independent C formulas, all observable bytes/canaries and per-configuration counters remain the executable oracles. The unchanged branch-only DAG proof removes the latch backedge/exit, admits no other external successors and processes all loop blocks from the header: the latch is the only sink and every entered iteration reaches it exactly once. For an unconditional recurrence, valid original SSA makes the contribution dominate its update. Existing recognition places that update in the latch or in an admitted diamond header; the header dominates the latch. Thus the contribution dominates the new latch scratch store. Exact use-edge closure excludes feedback from every moved accumulator or result into producer conditions, retained state, contributions or memory addresses. Every original producer branch, merge, guarded load/division/helper and original-memory operation stays in its original block/order. Chunking still requires a zero-start unit-step canonical IV with next-IV equality control in the admitted operand order, equality taking the exiting edge, and a finite representable count proof. Other affine/relational/reversed-equality controls retain full-trip-only admission. For an entered chunk, 0<=base<N and K=min(N-base,C)>0. The local ordinal resets to zero on every producer entry; exactly one latch visit increments it per original global iteration. Inductively i=0..K-1, so every scratch index is below K<=C; exit occurs at exactly K completed iterations. The unconditional consumer starts at slot zero and consumes exactly K initialized contributions in original iteration order, seeded by incoming chunk accumulators. Only then does base advance by K, without wrapping, before scratch reuse. Original nonidentity seeds and FP operand order/flags are preserved. Producer-state backedges are snapshotted before mutation and simultaneously forwarded through the dedicated producer exit; current, next, contribution and IV live-outs retain separate forwarding PHIs. All producer blocks remain mapped to the original inner loop and are added to the new chunk parent; existing ancestor membership, dedicated exits, topmost SE invalidation, DT rebuild and recursive LCSSA checks are unchanged. Exact original loop starts stay on stage preheaders and IDs through repeated LV. Strict ordinary FP and explicitly enabled fission FP reordering remain separate test rows; strictfp/constrained intrinsics and unsafe calls remain rejected. No fast-math, errno or additional numerical assumptions are added. The harness must execute actual transformed scalar/vector-tail modules against exact original IR plus an independent C traversal. New probes check actual branch edges and mixed-size scratch addresses/values per iteration, simultaneous incoming/final state, exact counts and actual vector/tail visits across boundaries.
costs: This revision adds validation code only; production scheduling, storage, operations, guards and analyses are unchanged from t000068. The fixture certificate builds small definition/predecessor maps and permits at most two scalar exit bridges and four PHI-forwarding steps; it is not a compiler equivalence engine or production analysis. The integration extension adds C=64/B=256 runs with one i32 store and load (4+4 logical bytes) per completed iteration; inherited full-trip C=65/B=260 runs remain. No generated input rereads, producer duplication or alias/versioning guards are added. Existing per-chunk min/select and producer/consumer/continuation branches remain. Production change: one admission-conjunct removal plus proof comments; no new analysis, CFG machinery, guards, memory accesses, streams or state arrays. Reuse the existing checked padded-capacity search (at most 64 steps over unique streams), entry allocations, min/remainder controller, local ordinal, scalar producer and ordinary-LV consumer. Storage is bounded independently of total runtime trips. New shared i32 plus double examples reserve alignTo(4*C,8)+8*C bytes: C=1/8/9/16/65 uses 16/96/112/192/784 bytes. Ceiling15 rejects a complete slot; ceiling111 fits C=8/B=96, ceiling112 fits C=9/B=112. The i32 stream feeds two sums with a single store/load stream. Logical traffic per completed original iteration is 12 bytes stored plus 12 loaded (24 bytes total), with no original input rereads, duplicated producer instructions or contribution recomputation. Three retained state carries and three reduction carries are reused. Original branch guards remain; canonical scheduling adds its existing per-chunk remaining<count select, producer latch/consumer latch and chunk continuation tests. No alias/versioning guards or compact empty-stream test is added for unconditional reductions. Code/analysis complexity remains the existing linear acyclic/effect/use/export analyses, LoopInfo membership over producer blocks and bounded capacity search. Validation adds four small original IR functions, extends the existing state certificate with original-block/latch awareness, adds two fixture-local branch/store probe hooks and one extra matrix. Validation-only input rereads/reference computations/probes are not compiler-generated traffic. Register pressure, stack-frame placement, spills, RVV execution, measured traffic and speedup are unmeasured.
limitations: No compiler, build, test runner, module verifier, host/RVV code generation, numerical execution or try.sh was invoked by this worker. AST parsing, source/immutable-output inspection and diff/whitespace checks only. All revised certificates, new mutation tests and numerical rows await independent harness execution. The previous t000068 build succeeded but two of 90 mandatory lit tests failed; later unit/execution/corpus checks were not established for that revision. The certificate intentionally recognizes this small fixture vocabulary and the observed LV1/LV2 scalar/tail/EVL layouts; future legal layout changes may require a new certificate case. Host fixed-vscale comparisons are not RVV execution; uninstrumented RVV machine verification/code generation is not measured speedup. No new numerical contract, FP/errno assumption, supported recurrence/CFG/control/effect shape or profitability policy is added. The production legality extension remains the inherited one-conjunct removal. d2 integration is assigned independently to t000069. Fresh primary outcomes, register pressure, physical traffic, spills and speedup remain unmeasured.
